answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may transact, like an ember that must stay lit to keep its place at the table. Creating thousands of fake identities then stops being free: every clone needs its own locked funds, and misbehaviour burns part of the stake. Honest agents crossing a cold tundra of low-trust strangers can still trade, because the stake proves commitment, while a single operator trying to flood a mesa of markets with sock puppets faces a cost that grows with every fake identity, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
